topic: Background agents - run_in_background, Monitor, SendMessage, Agent Teams

claims.claim: Three distinct async mechanisms exist: run_in_background (Bash one-shot), Monitor tool (event stream), Agent Teams + SendMessage (peer agents). Conflating them is the top community anti-pattern.
run_in_background is fire-and-complete (one notification at exit); not for streams. Community-stated defaults: 300s timeout, 50KB output buffer, 8-char UUID task ID.
Monitor tool shipped in Claude Code v2.1.98 on April 9, 2026. Event-driven: each stdout line = one notification; stderr routed to file not stream; silent = 0 tokens.
Monitor schema: 4 parameters - description (label), command (shell), timeout_ms (default 300000, max 3600000), persistent (boolean).
Monitor delivers ~95% token reduction vs polling for long watches (12k tokens polling -> <600 tokens Monitor for 10-min build watched at 15s intervals).
Monitor is unavailable on Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry - Anthropic API + Claude Code only.
Agent Teams requires Claude Code v2.1.32+ and CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 env var; released alongside Opus 4.6 on Feb 5, 2026.
Agent Teams architecture: team lead (main session) + teammates (separate Claude Code instances, own context) + shared task list + mailbox for peer messaging.
SendMessage tool supports 5 message types: message (direct), broadcast (all), shutdown_request, shutdown_response, plan_approval_response.
Subagent definitions can be reused as Agent Teams teammate types, BUT skills and mcpServers frontmatter are NOT applied when running as teammate (docs-documented asymmetry).
/resume and /rewind do not restore in-process teammates; lead may message non-existent teammate IDs after resume - fix is respawn.
Agent Teams hard limits: one team per session; no nested teams; lead is fixed for team lifetime; permissions set at spawn; shutdown is slow (finishes current tool call).
Split-pane mode NOT supported in VS Code integrated terminal, Windows Terminal, or Ghostty - requires tmux or iTerm2 (macOS-first).
Hooks for async work: SubagentStart (can inject context, cannot block), SubagentStop (can block), TeammateIdle (can block), TaskCreated (can block), TaskCompleted (can block).
async: true and asyncRewake: true hook flags (released January 2026) enable non-blocking hook execution - asyncRewake wakes Claude on exit code 2.
Team storage: config at ~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/config.json (runtime state, do not edit by hand); tasks at ~/.claude/tasks/{team-name}/. No project-level equivalent.
GitHub Issue #11716 (critical): background bash processes can cause infinite system-reminder loops and token exhaustion when output emits faster than session drains.
Recommended team size 3-5 teammates; broadcast costs scale linearly with team size - use targeted message by name instead.
TaskCompleted + exit code 2 is the canonical team-native quality-gate enforcement point: hook runs tests, blocks completion on failure.
Plan approval quality gate: teammate starts in read-only plan mode, sends plan_approval_response to lead, waits for approval; rejection includes feedback and triggers revision.

conflicts_flagged.description: Community confusion between run_in_background and Monitor; some posts use them interchangeably. They solve different problems (one-shot vs stream).
conflicts_flagged.resolution_hint: Synthesis must explicitly separate the three mechanisms.

gaps_flagged.description: run_in_background official schema not published in Anthropic docs - only community reverse-engineering.
Mailbox persistence semantics under teammate failure not explicit.
SubagentStart hook payload shape not fully published (SubagentStop is).
Task list file format inside ~/.claude/tasks/{team}/ not documented - cannot manually author or migrate.
No per-session token overhead measurement for teammates - community estimates 2x-10x single session, range too wide.
No documented pattern for a teammate using Monitor tool - presumably works but no example in docs.
